scope_note: External intentionally-vulnerable corpus from dineshshetty/Android-InsecureBankv2 (master branch prebuilt APK). Adopted to expand combined GT beyond MASTG, providing Java-side vuln density comparable to PleOS APKs. Intentional vulnerabilities are documented in the upstream README + various MASTG / OWASP MASTG references.

findings.title: Cleartext HTTP protocol hardcoded for login traffic
findings.rationale: Login credentials are POSTed via HttpClient with `protocol + serverip + ':' + serverport + '/login'` (line 98). HTTP is unencrypted, allowing MITM credential capture on any non-HTTPS path.

findings.title: Cleartext credentials logged on successful login
findings.rationale: Username + password concatenated into logcat. Any app with READ_LOGS (or a developer connected via adb) can recover credentials. Persistent on device until log buffer rotates.

findings.title: Hardcoded AES key string in source code
findings.evidence: String key = "This is the super secret key 123";
findings.rationale: 32-byte ASCII literal used directly as AES-256 key (CryptoClass.aes256encrypt/decrypt). APK reverse engineering yields the key, allowing decryption of all stored ciphertexts (e.g. SharedPreferences `superSecurePassword`).

findings.title: All-zero IV constant for AES-CBC
findings.rationale: AES-CBC with a fixed all-zero IV makes encryption deterministic across calls, enabling chosen-plaintext attacks and revealing whether two ciphertexts encrypt the same plaintext. CBC requires a fresh random IV per message.

findings.title: Exported receiver SMSes the decrypted password to a caller-supplied number
findings.rationale: Manifest declares `<receiver android:exported='true'>` for action `theBroadcast`. Any installed app can broadcast `theBroadcast` with extras `phonenumber` and `newpass` (line 17-18). The receiver decrypts the stored password and texts it to the attacker-supplied phone number — direct credential exfiltration via SMS.

findings.title: Exported ContentProvider with no read/write permission
findings.rationale: TrackUserContentProvider is exported without `android:readPermission` / `writePermission`. Any installed app can `query` / `insert` / `update` / `delete` records — login tracking + privacy leak.

findings.title: Exported broadcast receiver with no permission
findings.rationale: Receiver registered without `android:permission`. Combined with the action `theBroadcast`, any app can trigger the SMS-with-credential flow (see MyBroadCastReceiver finding above).

findings.title: Multiple internal activities marked exported=true (PostLogin / DoTransfer / ViewStatement / ChangePassword)
findings.rationale: These activities are post-login UI — should not be reachable from arbitrary external apps. Exported entry allows an attacker to launch them directly with crafted Intent extras, bypassing the login flow.

findings.title: WebView with JavaScript enabled in financial-statement view
findings.rationale: ViewStatement is exported (per manifest) and serves a WebView with JavaScript enabled. Combined with caller-supplied URL data, this is a XSS / credential-exfil sink via the financial statement screen.
